items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints
items.abstract_or_text: The worldwide escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe challenge to modern public health, necessitating novel classes of therapeutic agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent highly promising alternatives to small-molecule antibiotics due to their co-evolutionary resilience and rapid membrane disruption dynamics. However, translating computational AMP leads into clinical drug candidates remains bottlenecked by off-target cytotoxicity, predominantly hemolytic activity against mammalian erythrocytes. Although pretrained foundational protein language models (PLMs) have rapidly advanced molecular property prediction, current architectures frequently isolate antibacterial potency and cytotoxicity into disconnected single-task pipelines or succumb to catastrophic performance drops under strict homology-controlled evaluations. Recently, the Quantitative Mapping of Antimicrobial Peptides (QMAP) benchmark proposed that frozen PLM embeddings show weak linearly accessible features for hemolytic activity (HC50) resulting in poor rank correlation ({rho} < 0.25) on out-of-distribution sequence splits. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end multi-task parameter-efficient transfer learning framework designed to simultaneously optimize antibacterial potency and minimize mammalian cytotoxicity without sequence leakage. Built upon ESM-2 (150M), our architecture incorporates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) into self-attention projections, fine-tuning approx 0.70% of model weights. To restore gradient interference originating from disparate membrane lysis mechanisms, we implement an adaptive multi-task loss guided by Kendall homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. Evaluated across predefined QMAP benchmark splits enforcing a 60% maximal sequence identity threshold, our joint architecture remarkably outperforms conventional linear probes, tree-based regressors, and frozen foundational models. The framework achieves an E. coli potency rank correlation of {rho} = 0.6132 (r = 0.6816) and successfully elevates hemolytic toxicity correlation to {rho} = 0.5374 (r = 0.5541). To establish real world utility, we deploy the optimized joint network to screen a curated in silico library of 749 de-novo designed peptides, successfully isolating selective cationic-amphipathic candidates possessing Therapeutic Indices (TI = HC50/MIC) up to 144.03 while effectively deprioritizing broadly lytic motifs (TI < 2.0). These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation unlocks fine-grained bioactive structural semantics in foundational PLMs, providing an accurate, scalable framework for therapeutic peptide engineering.

items.title: AI-Guided Structure-Aware Modeling and Thermal Proteomics Reveal Direct Demethylzeylasteral-ACLY Interaction
items.abstract_or_text: Identifying the direct molecular targets of bioactive natural products remains a central challenge in chemical biology. Here we present an integrated experimental-computational framework, that combines matrix-augmented thermal proteomics with HoloGNN, a holistic graph neural network, to systematically prioritize and validate protein-ligand interactions. Benchmarking with PDBbind datasets HoloGNN achieves state-of-the-art performance. Applying this framework to 50 structurally diverse natural products identified Demethylzeylasteral as a direct interactor of ACLY. Orthogonal biochemical assays confirmed micromolar binding and enzymatic inhibition. In an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, Demethylzeylasteral reduced disease severity and inflammatory cytokine expression. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that Demethylzeylasteral reverses keratinocyte hyperproliferation and suppresses ACLY-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming. Together, this scalable, closed-loop strategy integrates thermal proteomics and machine learning to uncover direct targets of natural products and provides mechanistic evidence linking ACLY inhibition to therapeutic modulation of inflammatory pathology.

items.title: Decoding antibody-antigen recognition: the BL8 language and its application in calibrating deep learning predictions
items.abstract_or_text: Antibodies are central to immunology and therapeutics, and understanding how they recognize antigens is essential to rational drug design. This recognition depends on the interplay of interface geometry, physicochemical interactions, sequence context, and complementarity-determining region (CDR) conformation. However, traditional analyses often oversimplify this complexity, which becomes particularly problematic when evaluating the massive and frequently overconfident structural hypotheses generated by modern deep learning models. Here, we introduce BL8, an interpretable, eight-view structural language that comprehensively parameterizes interfaces across topology, shape, interaction, CDR conformation, flexibility, interfacial area, amino-acid-pair composition, and sequence background. Using 15,396 experimental interface records from the Structural Antibody Database (SAbDab), we built a fixed reference atlas containing 1,498 discrete BL8 signatures. The atlas shows that natural interfaces occupy a diverse, long-tailed structural space in which similar geometric scaffolds can be associated with different chemical and sequence features. Furthermore, we projected 28,501 predicted complexes involving programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD), and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1), generated using AlphaFold 3 (AF3), Protenix-v2, and OpenDDE, into the reference space. Acting as a robust underlying calibration layer, BL8 successfully decoupled physical viability from native confidence illusions, revealing cross-target hallucinations and filtering out 15.3% to 20.1% of highly deceptive false-positive predictions. Crucially, by benchmarking distinct generative behaviors across models, it enabled the extraction of highly reliable, multi-model consensus out-of-distribution binding paradigms. Together, BL8 bridges foundational biophysics with large-scale computational predictions, providing an essential benchmarking framework for discovering novel mechanisms in the era of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
items.abstract_or_text: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a potentially fatal toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates. Drug-safety studies in healthcare databases identify ILD with claims-based algorithms that trade positive predictive value (PPV) against sensitivity. We assessed whether large language models (LLMs) improve on these algorithms, with and without electronic health record (EHR) notes, and whether these gains translate into measurable epidemiological benefits. In 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes at Mass General Brigham, adjudicated by two pulmonologists, we compared 12 open-access LLMs with 20 published claims-based algorithms. LLMs received claims, EHR notes, or both, without task-specific training. Measures were PPV and yield (proportion classified positive). We projected the attenuation of a drug-induced ILD odds ratio under non-differential outcome misclassification. LLMs extended the PPV-yield frontier of the published algorithms with all three inputs. Across the 36 model--input evaluations, LLM PPV exceeded that of the best algorithm without specialist-coding requirements (Algorithm 4) by 14.3 percentage points on average. With claims alone, Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV (95% CI 78.2-95.6) at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% at 4.9% for the highest-PPV algorithm. With notes alone, Qwen3-32B achieved 78.9% PPV at 49.2% yield, versus 64.6% at 51.1% for Algorithm~4. With combined claims and notes, Qwen3-14B achieved 100.0% PPV at 24.3% yield. Under a simulated drug-safety scenario with a true odds ratio of 3.0, the projected observed odds ratio was 2.67 with combined inputs versus 1.07 with Algorithm 4, corresponding to a 46-fold difference in the estimated sample size required for 80% power (591 versus 27,200 patients). Zero-shot LLMs offer a higher-PPV alternative to rule-based claims phenotyping for ILD, on all three input types. Because the claims-only configuration uses the same claims data as existing algorithms, it could be deployed in administrative databases without linked notes, and may recover drug-safety signal otherwise lost to outcome misclassification.

items.title: Environment-Aware DNA Language Model for Stress-Responsive Genomic Prioritization in Maize
items.abstract_or_text: Abiotic stresses such as heat and drought severely reduce the productivity of major crops including maize, with adverse implications for agricultural sustainability. Despite progress in characterizing stress resilience, identifying genomic regions associated with stress response remains challenging due to complex genotype-by-environment interactions. Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), inspired by advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-training on DNA sequences to capture regulatory patterns; however, their adaptation to plant stress-response analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an environment-aware DNA-LLM framework that incorporates stress-specific prompt tokens into AgroNT, a transformer-based plant GFM, using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The model learns stress-conditioned genomic representations that exhibit distinct structures across environmental contexts. We further formulate a prioritization method that uses stress-induced shifts in these representations relative to the control condition together with stress-token-associated transformer attention patterns to identify putative stress-responsive genomic regions. The framework was evaluated on the Genomes-to-Fields (G2F) dataset, comprising over 4,000 maize hybrids grown across 38 locations over 8 years, using grain yield under heat, drought, and combined heat-drought stress. Flowering traits were used to assess generalizability of the stress-conditioned representations across phenotypes. The prioritized regions were assessed using spatiotemporal differential gene-expression profiles, stress-associated quantitative trait loci, and transcription-factor characterization. Regulatory motif analysis further revealed stress-associated motifs enriched within the prioritized sequences as well as model-emphasized high-attention regions. Functional annotation of genes proximal to prioritized regions highlighted roles in transcriptional regulation, signaling, and metabolic pathways relevant to abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of stress-conditioned transformer-based sequence modeling for environment-aware genome-to-phenome analysis in crop improvement.

items.title: Benchmarking DNA Foundation Models: Biological Blind Spots in Evo2 Variant-Effect Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: DNA foundation models such as Evo2 and DNABERT-2 show promise for variant-effect prediction (VEP), yet rigorous benchmarks assessing their ability to capture established biological constraints remain limited. Here, we introduce controlled benchmarks based on well-characterized nuclear and mitochondrial sequence features. Although Evo2 achieves strong aggregate performance on mitochondrial variants (AUROC = 0.927), our analyses reveal systematic blind spots in short-range signals, including codon usage bias, as well as spurious sensitivity to biologically neutral sequence context. Notably, changes in flanking sequences can cause pathogenic tRNA variants to be misclassified as benign. These findings suggest that Evo2's predictive performance may rely more heavily on learned sequence regularities than on the biological constraints governing variant function, raising concerns about the clinical utility of zero-shot genomic foundation models.Our framework provides a principled basis for standardized model evaluation and for guiding the development of architectures better aligned with biological constraints.

items.title: SMILE: A Structured Multi-Agent Clinical Reasoning for Liver Ultrasound Understanding
items.abstract_or_text: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. However, current generative vision-language models (VLMs) often rely on a single reasoning pathway that maps ultrasound appearance directly to textual descriptions. In addition to the inherent vision-language modality gap, this design is limited for liver ultrasound because disease interpretation is constrained by subtle visual evidence, heterogeneous disease patterns, and limited paired supervision. To address these limitations, we propose SMILE, a Structured Multi-agent clInicaL rEasoning framework that uses multiple complementary specialist agents to interpret ultrasound images and consolidates their outputs through a judge-guided consensus mechanism. Our approach employs three specialized agents: an image interpretation agent for morphological descriptions, a clinical-stage reasoning agent, and a visual question answering (VQA) agent for targeted queries. These agent responses are then aggregated and scrutinized by a judge VLM using a consensus filtering prompt to produce a unified, clinically coherent output. Across a public liver ultrasound dataset and an internal clinical dataset, SMILE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art VLMs, achieving up to 19.0\% improvement in ROUGE-1 and 18.8\% improvement in clinical F1-score, while reaching VQA F1-scores of 0.82 and 0.65 on public and internal datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of SMILE for data-scarce and limited-supervision clinical settings. Our models, datasets, and code are available https://github.com/CMME-Lab/SMILE{here}.

items.title: MedPsy: State-of-the-Art Small Medical Language Models for Efficient Edge Deployment
items.abstract_or_text: Medical language models promise expert clinical support, but the strongest open-source LLMs remain too large for private edge-device deployment, while compact medical models still trail substantially on knowledge-intensive and real-world healthcare tasks. Reasoning models that fit edge memory budgets can produce long reasoning traces, increasing sequential decoding, end-to-end latency, energy consumption, and KV-cache memory pressure. We present MedPsy, a family of text-only 1.7B and 4B medical language models designed for edge deployment, targeting this accuracy-generation-efficiency trade-off. Our recipe combines a synthetic medical data pipeline over biology, medicine, and health seeds with chain-of-thought targets from a 235B medical-focused LLM teacher; a four-stage post-training curriculum comprising two SFT stages followed by two RL stages with hard-sample mining; and an edge deployment evaluation spanning multiple GGUF quantization variants and real-device inference on laptop and smartphone hardware. On seven closed-ended medical benchmarks, MedPsy-4B surpasses MedGemma-1.5-4B by 19.34 points and matches MedGemma-27B while being 6.75x smaller; MedPsy-1.7B outperforms MedGemma-1.5-4B by 11.42 points despite being less than half its size. On HealthBench-Hard, MedPsy-4B surpasses MedGemma-27B by 15.33 points, while MedPsy-1.7B surpasses it by 11.66 points despite being ~16x smaller. Beyond accuracy, MedPsy reduces average response length by 1.7x (1.7B) and 3.2x (4B) versus its Qwen3 backbones, while Q4_K_M quantization preserves the aggregate score within 1 point of BF16 with ~69% lower disk footprint. In real-device inference, MedPsy-4B's shorter generations translate into 75% lower median end-to-end latency and estimated energy per answer than its Qwen3 backbone at matched quantization, while peak RAM remains below 5 GB across our tested laptop and smartphone configurations.

items.title: The DynaCell Evaluation Suite for Dynamic 3D Virtual Staining of Live Cells
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding how cells respond to perturbations over time is central to cell biology and drug discovery. Live-cell imaging captures the dynamics of perturbation-induced phenotypes in individual cells. While fluorescence imaging can visualize specific molecular phenotypes, labeling and repeated illumination often affect cell health. Virtual staining offers an alternative by predicting these fluorescence images from images acquired without fluorescent labels. Although many virtual staining models have been developed, their performance on volumetric time-lapse data remains poorly characterized. We address this gap with an evaluation suite for 3D time-lapse virtual staining of live cells. The suite combines paired 3D time-lapse images acquired with and without fluorescent labels, a set of baseline models, and three metric tiers measuring pixel-level fidelity, organelle segmentation performance, and single-cell phenotype similarity. Using this evaluation suite, we study metric and model behavior across 3 cell types, 2 microscopes, 4 organelles, and 3 perturbation states. We find that regression baselines better predict the spatial localization of target organelles, whereas the generative baseline better captures the distribution of phenotypes across cells. These differences expose trade-offs between structural and phenotypic fidelity that are obscured by single-metric evaluation and suggest how virtual staining models can be developed for diverse downstream tasks such as localization, segmentation, tracking, and phenotypic profiling. We release the curated datasets, baseline checkpoints, and evaluation code as part of DynaCell, a broader framework for image-based profiling of cell-state dynamics.

items.title: SE-BioNet: A Squeeze-and-Excitation CNN for Non-Invasive Overthinking Detection Using Biofield Imaging
items.abstract_or_text: Background: The human biofield has been explored as a possible indicator of physical and emotional states. Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) practices, such as Reiki, Therapeutic Touch, and Pranic Healing, incorporate biofield-related information into their assessment and therapeutic approaches. Gas Discharge Visualization (GDV) and Poly Contrast Interference Photography (PIP) are among the imaging techniques used to visualize biofield patterns. However, most existing studies have focused on GDV images, with comparatively limited research using PIP images and deep learning techniques. Overthinking is a growing mental health concern that is often difficult to identify using conventional diagnostic methods. This study explores whether deep learning can identify patterns in PIP biofield images associated with overthinking. Methods A convolutional neural network (CNN) integrated with a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism was developed for binary classification of biofield images into two classes: overthinking and no overthinking pattern. The SE module enhances discriminative feature learning by adaptively recalibrating channel-wise feature responses. The model was trained and evaluated separately on datasets annotated independently by two experts (Expert-I and Expert-II), and its performance was assessed using 5-fold cross-validation. Results The proposed SE-BioNet model achieved classification accuracies of 93.95% and 93.80% on Expert-I and Expert-II annotated datasets, respectively, with corresponding F1-scores of 94.02% and 93.59%. Five-fold cross-validation yielded mean accuracies of 92.22% ± 1.17% and 92.08% ± 1.34%, demonstrating stable generalisation. Conclusions The proposed framework demonstrates technical feasibility and consistent performance across cross-validation folds. However, validation using larger, multi-centre datasets is necessary to assess its generalizability. These findings highlight the potential of attention-based model in learning more useful features though further testing with larger datasets and expert validation is necessary for clinical application.

items.title: Deep Looking in Digital Pathology: An Explainable Federated Learning Framework for Lung Cancer Classification
items.abstract_or_text: Background: /Objectives: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and growing slide volumes add to pathologists’ cognitive load. Deep learning can assist histopathological diagnosis, but two obstacles limit its clinical use: privacy regulations keep patient images in institutional “data silos”, and the “black-box” behavior of neural networks undermines clinical trust. Inspired by Topol’s Deep Medicine, we aimed to build a diagnostic platform that preserves privacy and explains its decisions. Methods: We developed the Lung Cancer Analysis System (LCAS), which combines federated learning (FL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and a locally deployed medical large language model (LLM). Three public H&E datasets (LC25000, HistoSet-5×14, and CLID; 18,000 images; adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, benign tissue) acted as three hospital nodes with source-induced non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, and MobileNetV3-Small were trained centrally and with FedAvg/FedProx for 20 rounds. Grad-CAM produced visual evidence, and MedGemma 1.5, served offline through LM Studio, converted predictions and heatmap descriptors into structured reports. Results: Centralized training reached 99.50% ± 0.21% accuracy with DenseNet121. Under non-IID federated training with FedProx, DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B3 achieved 96.97% and 97.49% accuracy on an independent external blind test set of 958 images, whereas MobileNetV3-Small reached 91.23%. Accuracy remained 99.78% under Gaussian blur. t-SNE showed that global features clustered by tissue class rather than by hospital, and Grad-CAM highlighted glandular and tumor-nest regions consistent with histopathological criteria. Conclusions: FL, XAI, and on-premise LLM reporting can be integrated into a single workflow that keeps raw images within each institution while giving pathologists numerical, visual, and textual explanations, providing a practical path toward trustworthy cross-institutional computational pathology.

items.title: Accessed, never disclosed: Silent access to protected health information by medical artificial intelligence agents
items.abstract_or_text: Medical artificial intelligence agents should retrieve patient identifiers only when a task requires them, the data-minimization principle behind the HIPAA minimum necessary standard for protected health information (PHI). An agent can retrieve identifiers without revealing them. Such silent access remains invisible to evaluations that inspect only the output. We embedded canaries in synthetic patient records and linked each tool invocation to canary exposure in the final answers across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames for identifier-free clinical tasks. Three models invoked the PHI tools unnecessarily, whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 did not. Stronger boundaries reduced this access, and the residual access under the strictest policy was confined to frames in which the user overrode the policy or asserted approval. A pre-execution gate given the task-necessity criterion nearly eliminated this access. Output-only evaluation cannot verify minimum-necessary access; boundaries, gates, and access-log audits are required together.

items.title: FedEpitope: Parameter-Efficient Federated Protein Language Models for Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Linear B-cell epitopes are antigenic regions recognised by antibodies that play crucial roles in vaccine development, antibody production, and other therapeutic applications.Their prediction can support peptide-based vaccine candidate screening and diagnostic assay development, but the experimental data required for model development may be distributed across institutions that cannot freely pool their records. We present FedEpitope, a federated framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model for peptide-level linear B-cell epitope prediction using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping client-partitioned data local and restricting the communicated trainable model state to approximately 1.11 MB. Simulated benchmarks of FedAvg and FedProx algorithms, evaluated using homology-aware data splits of five biologically heterogeneous, organism-partitioned clients, achieve promising global test performance without centralising training data, with FedAvg outperforming all single-client models in mean AP, F1, and MCC. Additional experiments characterise post-federation personalisation, record-level differential privacy, sensitivity to controlled client heterogeneity, LoRA rank, and generalisation to the independent BCPreds and NetBCE benchmarks, demonstrating the feasibility of parameter-efficient federated protein language model adaptation for data-localised B-cell epitope prediction and the associated trade-offs among predictive performance, personalisation, privacy, communication efficiency, and distribution shift.

items.title: LabWeaver: reliable agentic data analysis grounded in laboratory knowled
items.abstract_or_text: Agentic systems powered by large language models are rapidly automating biological data analysis. However, their reliability remains questionable because they often overlook experimental context, such as disease domain and experimental protocol. Existing agentic systems organize context around individual users and projects, whereas research is organized around laboratories whose projects share experimental context. As a result, experimental context learned in one project remains unavailable to related projects. We introduce LabWeaver, an agentic data analysis framework with a laboratory-organized architecture of three tiers: laboratory, user and project. Further, LabWeaver distills experimental context into laboratory memory and skills, which are shared across users and projects after human-gated review. To isolate the contribution of experimental context, we analyzed a synovial sarcoma single-cell RNA-seq dataset in two sessions that differed only in whether laboratory memory and skills were available. The context-free session lost the fusion reporter at read alignment and misannotated the tumor cells. In contrast, the context-enabled session recovered reporter expression and resolved five fusion-anchored tumor cell states.

items.title: Benchmark of THReD: Evaluating an LLM Agent and Its Preprocessing Tools for Turning Electronic Health Records into AI-Ready Datasets
items.abstract_or_text: LLM agents are increasingly built into data-analysis software, yet little evidence shows how reliably they preprocess clinical data or whether the tools they invoke give correct, reproducible output. We report a benchmark of THReD, a web-based system that turns electronic health record (EHR) extracts into AI-ready datasets through a chat agent whose proposed steps run only after user confirmation. The agent benchmark has 141 tasks (100 templates) in seven categories, including goal-level requests, failure recovery, requests calling for no action, schema variation and prompt injection through the data, on synthetic tables calibrated to a regional health information exchange; success is judged by checks on the produced data. Over 2,550 episodes with Claude Haiku 5.5 in four context configurations, the deployed agent completed 92.7% (95% CI 88.1-96.4) of tasks on its first answer, abstained on every advice request, recovered from every injected fault, and never proposed an action requested by planted text. Without the data profile, completion fell to 58.0%; goal-level requests were hardest (80.6%). Six experiments on real records of two chronic-disease cohorts and on synthetic data at scale validate the tools: 91-92% of inferred patient classes and 99.7-99.8% of inferred vital-sign labels were correct in masked reconstruction; a dictionary builder combining curated dictionaries with LLM suggestions mapped 99.0% of 2,208 raw variants correctly; all 2,176 replays of 128 saved pipelines gave byte-identical files under pinned dependencies; subgroup differences in inference accuracy vanished within facility and lookup key; and the same-day consolidation rule changed 90-day emergency revisit rates by up to 3.2 points without shifting cohort composition by more than one point. Processing time grew roughly linearly to 5.5 million records while the prompt stayed at about 13 thousand tokens.

items.title: Uncovering the Multifaceted Role of the Kinetochore Scaffold 1 (KNL1) in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis and CRISPR-Cas9 Experimental Study
items.abstract_or_text: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by pronounced heterogeneity, chromosomal instability, and limited therapeutic options. Kinetochore scaffold 1 (KNL1), a core mitotic checkpoint component, is implicated in multiple cancers, but its role in HCC remains unclear. Here, we integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses with functional in vitro validation to elucidate the biological and clinical significance of KNL1 in HCC. KNL1 was markedly overexpressed in HCC tumors, particularly those harbouring TP53 mutations, and correlated with increased tumor break load, suggesting a link to structural chromosomal instability. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and hallmark gene set enrichment identified a KNL1-associated G2M checkpoint network, in which KNL1 ranked among the top 10 hub genes. A KNL1-G2M network score, stratified patients into high- and low-score groups, with high scores correlates with poorer overall survival, increased proliferation, and higher chromosomal instability. Immune deconvolution (CIBERSORTx) revealed that high-score tumors were enriched in T-regulatory cells and M0 macrophages, and had elevated TIDE and exclusion scores, indicating potential resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Single-cell RNA-seq confirmed preferential activation of the KNL1-G2M module in malignant hepatocytes and highlighted increased extracellular matrix remodeling and immunomodulatory interactions. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated KNL1 downregulation in HepG2 cells induced modest G2/M arrest, suppressed proliferation, reduced survivin and Bcl2 expression, and produced ultrastructural changes consistent with early apoptosis. Collectively, our results implicate KNL1 and its associated G2/M network in tumor progression-related processes, including chromosomal instability, proliferative activity, and immune modulation in HCC. While further mechanistic and clinical studies are required, KNL1 and its associated network may represent a biologically relevant vulnerability and a potential biomarker of aggressive disease behavior in hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Pharmacological activation of mitophagy prevents calcific aortic valve disease by targeting dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background and Aims: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) lacks pharmacologic therapy. Mitophagy impairment contributes to various degenerative diseases, but whether it occurs in calcified aortic valves and during human valvular interstitial cell (hVIC) osteogenic differentiation remains unknown. We therefore investigated the role of mitophagy in CAVD and whether its pharmacological treatment prevents disease progression. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on human aortic valves and hVICs. TJ0113, a novel orally available mitophagy activator from our previous screening, was tested in two CAVD mouse models. Multi-omics analyses and functional rescue experiments were performed to elucidate the mechanism. Results: Mitophagy was impaired in calcified human aortic valves and during hVIC osteogenic differentiation. TJ0113 activated MCL1-mediated mitophagy and attenuated disease progression in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the mitophagy receptor MCL1 anchors a fraction of PRMT3 on mitochondria. During osteogenic differentiation, a dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication is initiated by the increased release of PRMT3 into the cytosol, where it interacts with BACH1 and impairs BACH1 nuclear translocation. This leads to a widespread loss of BACH1 genomic occupancy, relieving BACH1-mediated transcriptional repression of the pro-osteogenic factor PARM1 and promoting hVIC osteogenic differentiation. Mitophagy activation by TJ0113 restored MCL1-PRMT3 binding and reversed these alterations. Conclusions: Mitophagy impairment drives CAVD through dysregulated mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication mediated by the MCL1-PRMT3-BACH1-PARM1 axis. Pharmacological mitophagy activation by TJ0113 corrects this communication and attenuates disease progression, representing a promising therapeutic strategy for CAVD.

items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.abstract_or_text: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

items.title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning models for electronic health records achieve strong predictive performance but provide little insight into what clinical concepts they represent internally. Post-hoc attribution methods produce per-cell importance scores that lack temporal coherence, cross-variable structure, and reusability across patients. We introduce the Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoder (TI-SAE), which learns a backbone-specific, patient-shared clinical concept dictionary from a frozen predictive model's representations. Each dictionary entry (latent) is defined by learned temporal Gaussian islands (specifying when the concept is active) and a sparse variable-composition vector (specifying which variables are involved). A decoupled selector then identifies which dictionary entries drive each patient's prediction, separating representation learning from attribution. We evaluate TI-SAE across five backbone architectures spanning different representation strategies on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV (three prediction tasks each). TI-SAE produces structured clinical concepts that go beyond transient attribution heatmaps while achieving strong performance on standard faithfulness benchmarks.

items.title: A single-cell multimodal foundation model enables cross modality analysis between transcriptome and chromatin
items.abstract_or_text: Most single-cell studies measure either gene expression or chromatin accessibility, and connecting the two usually requires fitting a model to each study. Here we present MUTUAL (MUltiome Transfer in a Unified Aligned Latent space), which keeps the single-cell foundation models scFoundation and EpiAgent frozen, combines their embeddings with linear summaries of each modality and learns a shared RNA--ATAC space from 3.0 million paired cells of 400 public multiome datasets. Applied without refitting to ten datasets not used for training, MUTUAL matched cells' RNA and ATAC profiles more accurately than methods fitted on other donors of the same dataset, annotated ATAC-only cells more accurately and transferred transcription-factor motif activity to RNA-only cells beyond what cell-type assignment provides. In a maturation series of stem-cell-derived islets, motif activity predicted from RNA largely reproduced the measured stage-wise changes when other libraries of the series served as the reference. MUTUAL makes public multiome data directly usable by single-modality studies.

items.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies BCHE and FOXM1 as oxidative-stress markers linked to prognosis and immune-microenvironment remodeling in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), an Epstein–Barr virus–associated head-and-neck cancer, typically carries dense yet dysfunctional immune infiltrates. Oxidative stress shapes both tumor progression and immune escape; whether oxidative-stress genes (OSGs) carry prognostic and immunological information in NPC has not been examined at bulk and single-cell resolution. Methods Three NPC microarray cohorts (GSE12452, GSE53819 and GSE64634) were integrated using robust rank aggregation and ComBat-corrected limma, and genes identified by both strategies were intersected with 1,398 OSGs from GeneCards. Candidate prognostic OSGs were tested in the RNA-seq cohort GSE102349 (n = 88) using univariate Cox, LASSO and multivariable Cox regression together with Kaplan–Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC curves and a nomogram. We further applied Hallmark gene-set enrichment, CIBERSORT, an immune-cell LASSO signature, checkpoint correlation, ssGSEA and drug-sensitivity prediction, and replicated the findings in three independent cohorts and a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE150430), where in-silico knockout, transcription-factor regulon, trajectory and cell–cell communication analyses were also performed. Results Of 722 consistent differentially expressed genes, 67 were NPC-specific OSGs. BCHE emerged as the consistently prognostic OSG (univariate HR = 1.85, P = 0.009; optimal-cutoff Kaplan–Meier P = 0.003, high-versus-low HR = 4.1; the sole LASSO-retained multivariable term). FOXM1 failed multivariable retention but still defined a high-risk subgroup by optimal-cutoff Kaplan–Meier (P = 0.012, HR = 4.4). Enrichment analysis tied FOXM1 to E2F/G2M/MYC proliferation programs and BCHE to epithelial–mesenchymal-transition and Wnt signaling; both genes were inversely related to interferon and complement pathways. A ten-cell immune signature and checkpoint correlations outlined an immune-suppressed compartment. At single-cell level, both genes localized to malignant cells within a shared early malignant state, and malignant–immune crosstalk was dominated by MIF- and galectin-mediated signaling. Conclusion Convergent bulk and single-cell evidence supports BCHE as a prognostic OS marker for risk stratification and FOXM1 as a proliferation-linked marker of malignant state in NPC. Both track with immune-microenvironment remodeling and await experimental and prospective validation.

items.title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have created opportunities for cross-lingual transfer of medical knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages to support access to healthcare information. However, medical question-answering (QA) datasets for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs remain scarce for Tetun. To address this gap, we translated MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information collections into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 medical QA pairs. Translation quality was assessed on 50 randomly sampled QA pairs (100 documents) using automatic metrics against human reference translations and evaluations by two native Tetun-speaking healthcare professionals, focusing on medical accuracy and Tetun fluency. Human translations achieved higher mean ratings than LLM-generated translations for both criteria (4.43/5 vs. 4.02/5), with statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To assess downstream utility, we fine-tuned Gemma and Llama variants on the translated MedAlpaca dataset using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and evaluated them on 325 Tetun-translated United States Medical Licensing Examination multiple-choice questions. Gemma 4 12B fine-tuned using QLoRA achieved relative improvements in mean accuracy of 10.79% with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) inference and 10.42% after merging the LoRA adapters into the BF16 base model, compared with the corresponding base models. These results highlight the viability of automatic dataset translation for Tetun medical QA and the effectiveness of PEFT in enhancing model performance. The datasets, models, and evaluation resources are accessible at https://github.com/labadain/labadain-medqa to support reproducible research on Tetun medical QA and facilitate machine translation, cross lingual, and multilingual research.

items.title: A candidate HNRNPU-CHD2 RNA-processing axis in neurodevelopmental disease
items.abstract_or_text: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in HNRNPU, which encodes a nuclear RNA-binding scaffold protein, cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, intellectual disability and brain malformations, but the programs that link HNRNPU dosage to neuronal dysfunction remain poorly defined. We depleted HNRNPU in Human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells, profiled gene expression and alternative splicing, intersected the two datasets, and asked which of the resulting genes already carried a neurodevelopmental annotation. Knockdown produced 5,643 differentially expressed genes and 21,728 high-confidence splicing events; 1,222 genes changed at both levels, and two pre-specified neurodevelopmental panel genes were among them: CHD2 and DYRK1A. In K562 eCLIP experiments, 107 reproducible HNRNPU peaks were detected across the CHD2 gene body, and three of the four regulated exons introduce a reading-frame shift whose premature termination codon lies far upstream of the final exon junction, predicting nonsense-mediated decay. Public K562 knockdown data reproduced the rise in CHD2 mRNA and the same skipped-exon change, and CHD2 depletion in the neural line SH-SY5Y altered cell-cycle, DNA-repair and neural gene programs. HNRNPU therefore constrains a frameshift-prone splicing switch in CHD2, a candidate route from HNRNPU haploinsufficiency to loss of functional CHD2 if these transcripts are degraded.

items.title: Bayesian Sequential Optimal Experimental Design for Single-Pixel Imaging using Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Adaptive compressed sensing (CS) aims to select the most informative measurements sequentially, which is crucial for many modern imaging systems. This task can be formulated as a Bayesian sequential optimal experimental design (sOED) problem, where each new acquisition is chosen to maximally reduce uncertainty about the unknown image given prior information and subsequent data provided by acquisitions. However, in single-pixel imaging (SPI), the large design space consists of all possible binary illumination patterns. Directly optimizing the Bayesian sOED objective over this space using conventional methods is generally challenging. In this work, we reformulate sOED for SPI as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. In RL, an agent learns a policy through repeated experimental trials to maximize a reward, here given as the expected information gain, the most complete measure of uncertainty reduction in Bayesian OED. This avoids the need to directly optimize complex information-theoretic objectives during a measurement to obtain the next design. Instead, the result is a learned policy function that directly maps the current posterior belief about the image to the next optimal binary measurement pattern, in a computationally efficient way. Using a simple yet representative SPI imaging scenario, this work evaluates the scalability of the learned policy under two different policy parameterizations. Furthermore, we investigate how performance deteriorates when only approximate posterior information is available or the measurements are impaired by noise, and propose several strategies to introduce additional design constraints motivated by biomedical applications. The numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian sOED-RL framework remains robust and can be extended to more complex, large-scale SPI scenarios.

items.title: Kinetics and Evolution-guided Design of High Fidelity CRISPR-Cas Endonucleases
items.abstract_or_text: Finding high-fidelity CRISPR-Cas variants is critical for both the precision of in vitro DNA detection and the safety of in vivo gene-editing therapeutics. However, the large size of the Cas enzymes and the distinct selection criteria between its natural evolution and clinical practice lead to extensive experimental trials and limited success rate for de novo design, directed evolution and protein language model (PLM)-based filtering. Here, we present a physics-driven, PLM-assisted approach that utilizes atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and automated path searching to efficiently obtain the atom-level kinetic insights, including the transition state structures, for the conformational changes of R-loop formation that dictate the off-target DNA recognition and cleavage by Cas. We show that these kinetic insights can pinpoint the fidelity-diminishing protein residues during the early stage of target recognition. Integrated with PLM-filtering of the mutants on these sites, this approach identified high-fidelity SpyCas9 and FnCas12a variants (4.49-fold and 6.69-fold increase respectively from wild-type), surpassing previously reported counterparts at minimal cost of only a few wet-lab validations (cellular genome-editing and ribonucleoprotein cleavage assays respectively).

items.title: Human-Governed Multi-Agent AI for Biological Hypothesis Generation: An Evidence-Grounded Framework Using JUMP Cell Painting Profiles
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract High-dimensional cellular phenotypes can motivate biological hypotheses, but similarity alone cannot establish mechanism or causal validity. DISCOVERY-AGENT links exploratory JUMP Cell Painting evidence with evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, independent critique and bounded human-review routing. An initial 65-record CRISPR/ORF analysis across nine gene–modality tests found four FDR-significant CRISPR plate-level associations (AKT1, BRCA1, MTOR and TP53), none among evaluated ORF genes. A distinct later cross-source compound-identity benchmark used 614 morphological features and achieved AUROC 0.6142 on 1,250 held-out compounds with training-only preprocessing; this is identity discrimination, not mechanism-of-action classification. Three structured hypotheses underwent LLM critique and revision, while eleven gene-pair evidence assessments yielded no FDR-significant mechanistic finding (minimum q = 0.2037). Archived governance checks passed 1,021/1,021 predefined tests; nevertheless, the initial live-agent run contained two execution errors among five cases, with both cases responding on fresh retest. These findings demonstrate feasibility of auditable evidence processing and modest cross-source morphology signal, not validated autonomous discovery, prospective safety, or completed expert review. The work delineates practical requirements for independent biological validation and reproducible scientific agents.

items.title: A collaborative submission model for building high-quality data resources at scale through partnership: lessons from single-cell genomics
items.abstract_or_text: Community data resources that aggregate datasets across studies are critical infrastructure for modern biomedical research, accelerating discovery, and rapidly-advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) models place ever-greater demand on large, well-described data corpora. However, building these resources involves a fundamental tension: comprehensive metadata is imperative for reuse, yet capturing this information systematically requires substantial effort that limits growth. We detail how CZ CELLxGENE Discover has used a collaborative submission model, whereby data contributors partner with dedicated resource curators, to become a large, widely used single-cell genomics resource for diverse analytical applications including AI model development and integrative analysis. This partnership leverages contributors' intimate study knowledge and curators' focus on data reuse and expertise in standardization to improve data quality, metadata accuracy, and richness. This is achieved by motivating researcher participation through tangible benefits while minimizing submission burden. We contrast this collaborative model with contributor-driven and resource-driven approaches, highlighting tradeoffs in scalability, consistency across submissions, and quality assurance. The principles and practices we describe provide a framework for building high-quality community data resources across diverse biological data types.

items.title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Screening Framework for Efficient Eligibility Evaluation of Clinical Trial Patients
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Clinical trial patient eligibility screening is a core and labor‑intensive step in clinical research, which traditionally relies on manual review of electronic health records (EHRs) and suffers from high time costs, human errors, and inconsistent screening criteria. With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), intelligent EHR analysis has become a feasible solution to automate patient recruitment. However, existing single‑LLM inference and single‑agent screening methods often fail to parse complex inclusion and exclusion rules, yielding unstable prediction and substantial false‑positive or false‑negative outputs. Methods This paper proposes a modular multi‑agent collaborative framework built upon LangGraph for clinical trial patient eligibility evaluation. The workflow is decomposed into four specialized agents. LLMs are only used for unstructured text understanding, while eligibility matching adopts deterministic rule‑driven computation to avoid LLM output randomness. Retrospective simulation experiments are conducted on an in‑house programmatically generated synthetic EHR cohort. Results Our multi‑agent framework achieves perfect accuracy, precision, recall and F1‑score on simulation cohort, outperforming the end‑to‑end single‑agent baseline. Conclusions This work provides a proof‑of‑concept intelligent automation paradigm for clinical‑trial patient screening validated on an in‑house synthetic EHR cohort; further real‑world clinical validation is required before practical clinical deployment, and the framework can be further migrated toward multicenter and cross‑border clinical trial recruitment scenarios.

items.title: Capacity Planning for Resource-Constrained Clinical LLM Serving
items.abstract_or_text: Deploying large language models (LLMs) under a fixed accelerator budget requires jointly deciding how computational capacity is allocated across model sizes and how incoming requests are routed across that capacity. Although prior work has extensively studied LLM routing and serving efficiency, the relative importance of fleet composition and routing under resource constraints remains less understood. We investigate this question using a controlled four-GPU serving environment with heterogeneous clinical NLP workloads spanning short factual verification, biomedical semantic matching, and long-context clinical summarization. We systematically vary fleet composition, routing policy, and offered load while holding the workload trace and hardware budget fixed. Across 24 configurations, descriptive main-effect shares attribute more variation to fleet composition than to the evaluated routing policies in time to first token, latency, and long-context coverage. All-small fleets provide the best responsiveness and throughput but substantially lower long-context coverage, whereas larger-model capacity improves coverage at the cost of serving efficiency. Heterogeneous fleets provide intermediate operating points but can introduce strong-model bottlenecks when large-model capacity is scarce. In a focused evaluation of this bottleneck, capacity-aware routing reduces mean latency and increases throughput while incurring a small reduction in long-context coverage. Within this measured regime, the results support prioritizing capacity allocation, with routing managing demand within the provisioned capacity.

items.title: Agentic Discovery Transfer Enables Cross-Cancer Discovery at Scale
items.abstract_or_text: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested as doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing studies. Given a source manuscript and a target dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and mechanistic findings, generates and executes analyses for the testable findings, reports which findings transfer, and suggests follow-up. Applied to 121 studies across six cancer types, SMART identified findings that transfer across cancers, including a lung cancer prognostic signature that we confirmed to be associated with survival in liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and pleural mesothelioma. SMART also generated new mechanistic hypotheses, demonstrating how agentic discovery transfer can extend published findings beyond their original setting.

items.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq
items.abstract_or_text: Summary: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-discriminative signals. Selected regions are used to generate a gene-by-cell activity matrix. Across 196 paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets, VIGAT outperformed five existing methods in recovering marker-associated accessibility enriched in the corresponding cell populations, demonstrating the utility of VLM-guided visual reasoning for scalable gene activity quantification. Availability and implementation: VIGAT is implemented as an open-source R package and is freely available at https://github.com/beijie02/VIGAT.

items.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
items.abstract_or_text: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

items.title: RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs
items.abstract_or_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) has improved the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across a wide range of tasks. However, token-level RL assigns an action's advantage to the entire generated response, including tokens specifying the parsed action, reasoning chains, and malformed content. Although the environment executes only the parsed action, variation in how the action is expressed in natural language can introduce additional variance into policy-gradient estimates. We propose RLiD (Reinforcement Learning in the Decision plane), a framework that directly optimizes the probabilities of executable action options. RLiD compiles observations, an optional compact memory, and a labeled action menu into the model input, and uses a large decision model (LDM) to select an action in a single forward pass. By eliminating autoregressive token generation and bypassing action parsing, RLiD avoids invalid action outputs and improves RL rollout efficiency. Our analysis shows that, within a fixed text policy, marginalizing over alternative realizations of the same action removes a zero-mean gradient component without changing the expected update. We further distill trained LDM policies into generative LLMs through supervision on their action trajectories. Experiments on ARC, Countdown, and Sokoban demonstrate improved performance or lower computational cost across several settings. On ALFWorld, the complete training and distillation pipeline reaches 99.3% success in 12.7 H100 GPU-hours, compared with 86.6% in 17.3 GPU-hours for token-level RL of the same LLM. With compiled memory, our strongest Qwen2.5-1.5B LDM and distilled generative LLM achieve 100% success on all 134 unseen and 140 seen ALFWorld evaluation games.

items.title: HNRNPC-mediated RNA processing promotes VHL-associated excessive vasculogenesis in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome revealed from patient-derived blood vessel models
items.abstract_or_text: Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome (VHLS) is an inherited disorder characterized by excessive vascularization, which contributes to the development of hemangioblastomas and benign or malignant tumors, as well as renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and cysts in multiple organs. VHLS is caused by mutations in VHL tumor suppressor gene, which encodes a component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. Although therapeutic agents targeting hypoxia-inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF2A), which is stabilized by VHL loss and promotes tumor angiogenesis, have been approved for clinical use, their therapeutic response remains limited in RCC patients associated with VHLS. Therefore, there is an unmet need for the development of alternative therapeutic approaches independent of HIF2A. Here, we establish a human iPSCs-based model of VHLS-associated excessive vasculogenesis using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from VHLS patients and VHL-edited isogenic iPSC lines. Vascular cells (VCs) differentiated from these VHLS-specific iPSCs exhibited excessive blood vessel formation compared to healthy donor-derived VCs, leading to vascular lesion formation characterized by abundant blood vessels and abnormal cellular growth in vivo. Mechanistically, RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) were preferentially stabilized in the patient-VCs. Among these RBPs, the stabilization of heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein C1/C2 (HNRNPC), which is a substrate for pVHL-mediated protein degradation independent of HIF2A expression, was critical for the dysregulated vascularization caused by VHL inactivation in this model. These findings provide an iPSCs-derived vascular platform to elucidate VHLS mechanisms and identify HNRNPC as a potential therapeutic target for VHL-driven vascular lesion formations through an HIF2A-independent mechanism.

items.title: METTL15-mediated m4C modification regulates glucose metabolic reprogramming in a c-Myc translation-dependent manner and promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract HCC is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Metabolic reprogramming, particularly enhanced glycolysis, is a hallmark of HCC progression, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. METTL15, a m4C RNA methyltransferase, has recently been implicated in mitochondrial function, but its role in HCC is largely unknown. In this study, we reveal that METTL15 is significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and cell lines, and its high expression correlates with unfavorable clinical outcomes. Functional assays demonstrate that METTL15 promotes HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, METTL15 enhances glycolytic flux by facilitating the translation of the oncogene c-Myc in an m4C-dependent manner, thereby driving glucose metabolic reprogramming. Knockout of METTL15 suppresses glycolysis and attenuates c-Myc protein expression without affecting its mRNA levels, suggesting a post-transcriptional regulatory axis. Our findings identify METTL15 as a novel epitranscriptomic regulator of glucose metabolism in HCC and highlight its potential as a promising therapeutic target.

items.title: Australian isolates of cell fusing agent virus and Culex flavivirus provide new tools to study insect-specific flaviviruses
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Cell fusing agent virus (CFAV) and Culex Flavivirus virus (CxFV) represent the prototype insect-specific flaviviruses (ISFs) found in Aedes and Culex species, respectively. While these viruses have been isolated from mosquitoes on several different continents, no isolates have been reported from Australian mosquitoes. In this study we successfully isolated CFAV from Aedes aegypti originating from Cairns in North Queensland, Australia and CxFV from Culex quinquefasciatus collected from Brisbane in South-East Queensland, representing the first field isolates for both viruses from Australia. Phylogenetic analysis of these isolates revealed that the new CFAV isolates were closely related to CFAV sequences previously detected by deep sequencing of pools of Aedes aegypti collected in North Queensland, while the genome sequences of the Brisbane CxFV isolates were most closely related to isolates of CxFV from Culex quinquefasciatus collected from Mexico in 2008. Using these Australian isolates, we report the first infectious clone created for CFAV, and the first infectious clone of the Australian strain of CxFV. Growth kinetics revealed that infectious clones of CFAV and CxFV replicated more efficiently than their wild-type counterparts, reaching titres more than 10 8 TCID 50 /ml. Deep-sequencing of these isolates indicated that differences in replication were due to co-infections of mosquito-derived native viruses with other viruses absent in infectious clone stocks. Using a panel of novel monoclonal antibodies raised against the CFAV virion proteins, we demonstrated antigenic relatedness between CFAV and CxFV and other lineage I ISFs, particularly those carrying the conserved FKW motif at positions 106–108 in the fusion loop region of the viral envelope protein. All generated mAbs bound CFAV with one mAb additionally recognising the ISFs CxFV, Palm Creek virus (PCV), Parramatta River virus (PaRV) and Niénokoué virus (NIEV). While these mAbs did not bind CxFV and CFAV proteins in mosquitoes injected with the infectious clones, the first immunofluorescence analysis of disseminated of CFAV in Aedes mosquitoes was visualised through anti-dsRNA staining, showing widespread infection across multiple mosquito tissues, including the midgut and ovaries. These advancements in the development of elementary tools provide opportunity to further our understanding of ISFs and pave the way for their potential application in laboratory research, as well as innovative mosquito-borne disease control strategies.

items.title: Accounting for Irregular State Transitions through Belief Estimation in Online Medical Consultation
items.abstract_or_text: While online medical consultation broadens access, unprompted patient disclosures and topic shifts frequently disrupt clinician inquiry, leaving clinical states progressively revealed. We characterize these dynamics using both existing evaluation metrics and task-specific interaction metrics designed in this work. Through an empirical study across 16 medical dialogue datasets, we show that authentic online interactions exhibit substantially lower contextual continuity and higher unpredictability than offline and simulated benchmarks. We propose PRISM (Policy Reasoning with Inferred States for Medicine), a framework inspired by partially observable Markov decision processes that decouples latent state estimation from action selection to address drifting dialogue trajectories. Specifically, PRISM factorizes clinical triage into belief estimation, policy optimization, and response realization. By maintaining an evolving posterior belief over consultation states and conditioning action selection on the maximum a posteriori state, PRISM advances clinical goals while accommodating patient-initiated shifts. Extensive evaluations show that PRISM substantially outperforms frontier LLMs and clinical agents, achieving a 22.40 percentage point gain in clinical decision accuracy alongside decisive improvements in response generation, surpassing the strongest baseline by 5.51 points in BERTScore_F1. Furthermore, ablation studies show that providing oracle consultation states consistently boosts response quality across all evaluated baselines by guiding their action reasoning, yielding average gains of 5.58 points in BERTScore_F1.

items.title: Development and Internal Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Predicting Postoperative Delirium in Older Adults Undergoing Orthopaedic Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Objective Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious complication following hip or knee replacement and revision surgery in older patients, leading to prolonged recovery, increased healthcare costs, and poor long-term outcomes. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine learning (ML)-based risk prediction model for POD using multidimensional perioperative variables and to compare the predictive performance of seven ML algorithms. Methods This single-center prospective observational cohort study included 930 older patients (≥ 60 years) who underwent elective hip or knee replacement and revision surgery. POD was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) within 7 days after surgery. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection. Seven ML algorithms were developed and compared, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretability. Results POD occurred in 30.0% (279/930) of patients. LASSO identified six predictors: preoperative sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI), psychological distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale, K10), social support (Groningen Orthopaedic Social Support Scale, GO-SSS), nutritional status (Prognostic Nutritional Index, PNI), comorbidity burden (age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, aCCI), and intraoperative physiological reserve (Surgical Apgar Score, SAS). The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model performed best, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.922 (95% CI : 0.886–0.957) and a Brier score of 0.095. SHAP analysis revealed that preoperative sleep quality was the most influential predictor, showing a nonlinear positive association with POD risk and a synergistic interaction with psychological distress. Conclusion The XGBoost-based model integrating six readily available predictors demonstrated good predictive performance and potential clinical utility. The SHAP-based interpretability enhances model transparency, supporting early risk identification and personalized perioperative management. External validation is warranted to confirm generalizability.

items.title: Characterization of the frameshift c.515dupC knock-in mouse model of HSPB8-associated myopathy (MFM13) and evaluation of Trehalose as autophagy modulating therapy.
items.abstract_or_text: Heat shock protein family B member 8 (HSPB8) is a chaperone involved in the chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA) complex. HSPB8 in conjunction with cochaperone Bcl2-associated athanogene 3 (BAG3), promotes autophagy-mediated removal of misfolded proteins associated with various neurodegenerative diseases. Mutations in HSPB8, previously associated with Charcot Marie Tooth disease type 2L, have recently been linked to an autosomal dominant rimmed vacuolar myopathy (MFM13), and is considered a multisystem proteinopathy. Patients have distal and proximal limb girdle myopathy with muscle biopsy showing fatty replacement, endomysial fibrosis, and rimmed vacuoles leading to muscle atrophy and early demise. We have demonstrated reduced expression of HSPB8, altered autophagy, and TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) accumulation in patient fibroblasts. Overexpressed murine Hspb8 frameshift mutant (c.515dupC, fs) displays insolubility and aggregation propensity in Murine Neuroblastoma X Spinal Cord 34 (NSC-34) cells. Using clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) technology, we generated a knock-in Hspb8 mouse model of the c.515dupC hot spot frameshift variant to study disease pathology. Mutant Hspb8 mice developed late onset muscle weakness beginning at 15 months. Muscle biochemical analyses revealed reduced HSPB8 levels, increased TDP 43, and altered autophagy markers, partially recapitulating the human phenotype. Fiber type analysis, neuromuscular junction integrity, and motor neurons show mild myopathy without neurodegeneration. Given the lack of available treatments, we evaluated trehalose, a natural disaccharide that is known to induce HSPB8 and enhance autophagy as a potential therapy. Administration of 2% trehalose in the drinking water restored HSPB8 expression; however, it did not significantly ameliorate autophagic dysfunction or TDP-43 pathology in mutant mice. These findings support the value of our preclinical models for translational studies, and autophagy enhancement as a potential therapeutic strategy for HSPB8-related myopathy.

items.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows us to effectively regularize the landscape with activations from brain regions or neural network units. Our model Vis-Lens integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model into an image generation framework. It enables the generation of natural, realistic preferred images by directly modifying the activation-regularized latent codes without per-image iterative optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on both artificial neural networks and human visual cortex using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Our framework improves activation modulation and image realism compared with a recent state-of-the-art method for generating preferred visual representations of these neural targets.

items.title: Attribution-based diagnostics for single-cell foundation models
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell RNA foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for in-silico biological discovery, yet predictive performance alone does not reveal whether their decisions rely on biologically meaningful signals or model-specific shortcuts. We systematically investigate post-hoc attribution of downstream predictions across two tasks: cell-type annotation using pretrained Cell2Sentence and scGPT models, and perturbation prediction using scGPT+STATE in a controlled setting. For cell annotation, we use attribution to assess whether predictions rely on established marker genes and how their relevance varies with model architecture, expression rank, and the surrounding cellular context. For perturbation prediction, we compare attribution patterns with known regulatory ground-truth in a synthetic setting to assess what they reveal about the model's learned computations. Across these tasks, attribution reveals biological feature use, contextual interactions, contributions from different input pathways, learning progression, associations with prediction quality, and potential pitfalls that are not fully captured by standard performance metrics. Experiments with complete and limited regulatory knowledge further demonstrate that conclusions drawn from attribution depend strongly on the choice of biological reference, baseline, and null model. Together, these findings highlight the value of attribution as a flexible post-hoc diagnostic for understanding model behavior, identifying potential issues, and informing the development of scFMs.

items.title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
items.abstract_or_text: Background. Testing and deploying medical AI systems at scale already results in more outputs than clinicians can review, and the use of large language models (LLMs) as judges is growing rapidly. Decision-only models, cheap and fast models that return structured probabilities rather than text, offer a potentially scalable option for that goal. Methods. In an OSF pre-registered evaluation, we tested TypeSafe Jev 1.13 as a judge on tasks from five validated clinical benchmarks: rubric grading (HealthBench), planted clinical errors (When Rubrics Fail), risk in AI-written clinical documents (MedVAL), counseling ratings and failures (CounselBench) and physicians' preferences between answers (Real-POCQi). Comparators were expert raters' agreement with each other, OpenAI Decisions, GPT-6 Luna, a proposed hybrid team combining decision models and a cheap LLM and, as frontier comparators, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. The main outcome was plain agreement with the expert label. Results. The test comprised 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls. Jev's agreement with expert labels averaged 64.7% over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US1.46; per judgment, it cost 1/34 of Sol's price and 1/152 of Opus's. A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev's least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit. Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Conclusions. Across more than 200,000 model calls, a decision-only model was non-inferior to two frontier judges on most tasks at a small fraction of their cost and time, while reporting how sure it was of every call. With local cutoffs and expert oversight of omissions and clinical documents, judging every output of a deployed medical AI system becomes more affordable.

items.title: Deep learning grading of Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images: a weighted soft-voting ensemble of convolutional and transformer networks
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Schistosomiasis morbidity still persists in China despite extensive progress towards elimination of new and active infections. Diagnosis of liver fibrosis related to Schistosoma japonicum remains challenging due to the subjective nature of ultrasound grading and the shortage of experienced sonographers in endemic counties. Methods: We developed a deep learning model that grades schistosomal liver fibrosis from a single B-mode ultrasound image without manual delineation of a region of interest. We used 2,921 images from 2,921 adults (aged 18-88 years, median age 54 years; 46.4% female) from a schistosomiasis hospital in Jiangxi Province, China, between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 12.9%, 34.6%, 32.4% and 20.2% had grade 0, 1, 2 and 3 fibrosis, respectively. Fibrosis grades were based on the clinical ultrasound record and re-evaluation by an experienced radiologist according to the Chinese Handbook of Schistosomiasis Control; discordant cases were reviewed by a second radiologist and resolved by consensus. Predictions from four neural networks with different architectures (ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T) were combined by weighted soft voting, with weights derived from validation performance. Results: For the four-grade task this model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184-0.8856), an accuracy of 0.8500 (0.8136-0.8818) and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9187 (0.8983-0.9373) on a fixed test set of 440 images. For detecting significant fibrosis (grade 2 or 3; test-set prevalence 0.530), sensitivity was 0.9700, specificity was 0.9179, positive predictive value was 0.9300, negative predictive value was 0.9645, and AUROC was 0.9817. The ensemble achieved a higher macro-F1 than each individual backbone. Every ensemble misclassification was to an adjacent grade; no image with severe fibrosis was classified as no or mild fibrosis, or vice versa, whereas each individual backbone made 1-4 errors spanning two or more grades.
