Conclusions: The model may provide an automated aid for Schistosoma japonicum-associated fibrosis grading and could potentially support screening and follow-up in endemic areas after external validation.

items.title: Multi-Agent Learning for Adaptive Prompt Optimization in Heterogeneous Clinical Narratives
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Free-text narratives within electronic health records, particularly echocardiography reports, contain vital physiological parameters that are frequently absent from structured flowsheet tables. While modern foundation language models offer strong textual comprehension, manual prompt engineering remains an empirical and non-robust procedure. Small prompt changes can cause formatting errors, missed unit conversions, and numerical hallucinations. To address these issues, we formulate prompt optimization as a discrete-action Markov Decision Process and evaluate it on 120,555 echocardiography notes from 38,022 adult ICU patients in the MIMIC-IV database. Unlike conventional rule-based parsers and naive prompts, the proposed reinforcement learning agents optimize extraction using a numeric reward with a strict \pm 2.5% relative tolerance. Both the off-policy Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) and on-policy Deep SARSA agents converged within 15 training episodes, achieving a 7.24% relative improvement in extraction accuracy over conventional NLP methods.

items.title: BioGraphX-Sol: A Structure-Free, Fully Interpretable Protein Solubility Predictor Exceeds AlphaFold3-Based Methods and Reveals Nine Universal Cross-Species Determinants
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Protein solubility is a critical determinant of recombinant expression yield, yet current state-of-the-art predictors often rely on either AlphaFold3-predicted structures or large ensembles of protein language models, limiting accessibility and interpretability. We present BioGraphX-Sol, a sequence-only predictor that constructs biophysically grounded constraint graphs directly from amino acid sequences to extract 200 physicochemical features spanning graph topology, IDP and polymer physics, aggregation-hotspot geometry, and novel surface- and terminal-conditioned descriptors, without requiring 3D coordinates, multiple sequence alignments, or pretrained models. On the standard eSOL benchmark, the XGB+ESM post-hoc ensemble essentially matches ProtSATT in predictive performance (R^2 = 0.5451 vs.\R^2 = 0.5450), despite training only 1.44M neural parameters and requiring no structure prediction. The physics-only XGBoost configuration (R^2 = 0.499, ROC--AUC = 0.873) exceeds FGNNSol (R^2 = 0.487, ROC--AUC = 0.867), which combines AlphaFold3-derived 3D coordinates with ESM-C embeddings and structural descriptors across roughly 1,831 input dimensions, showing that explicit 3D structure prediction is unnecessary when the relevant physicochemical information is correctly encoded. A post-hoc \alpha sweep quantifies the physicochemical-to-evolutionary information balance at approximately 59\%/41\%, providing, to our knowledge, the first quantitative decomposition of information sources for protein solubility prediction. In zero-shot transfer to S.\cerevisiae, the physics-only XGBoost achieves the highest ROC--AUC (0.8524) and PR--AUC (0.9246) among all evaluated methods. Permutation-importance analysis identifies nine universal solubility determinants exhibiting consistent directional effects across E.\coli and S.\cerevisiae (9/9 agreement). The physics-only configuration requires no GPU at inference and runs efficiently on standard CPU hardware, supporting the Green AI principle that compact, interpretable representations grounded in domain knowledge can provide a viable alternative to parameter scaling.

items.title: Deciphering Accelerated Biological Ageing in Breast Cancer Survivors and Cancer-Free Women Using Explainable Machine Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Purpose Breast cancer survivors are at increased risk of accelerated biological ageing, yet the interconnected variables driving this process remain poorly mapped. This study aimed to decipher the multidimensional factors associated with accelerated biological ageing using explainable Machine Learning (ML) architectures. Methods As part of the Cancer Survivors’ Trajectories of Ageing Research (C*STAR) study, a cross-sectional analysis was conducted among 262 breast cancer survivors and 262 cancer-free controls. Ageing phenotypes, behavioural lifestyle factors, sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were assessed, utilising absolute telomere length as the primary ageing biomarker. An XGBoost model integrated with the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Regression with Gaussian Noise (SMOGN) was optimised using Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) to map non-linear associations, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evaluated feature importance. Results The XGBoost-SMOGN pipeline substantially reduced the mean absolute error for breast cancer survivors (0.0070 vs. 0.1785) and controls (0.0074 vs. 0.1592) compared to native models. As synthetic sampling was applied globally, these metrics reflect internal feature mapping rather than generalisable predictive accuracy. SHAP analysis deciphered that accelerated ageing (shortened telomeres) in survivors was primarily associated with impaired functional status, excessive sleep, high stress, radiotherapy, and high processed meat consumption. Paradoxically, optimal cognitive status and shorter sitting durations were also linked to accelerated ageing in survivors. Decelerated ageing in survivors correlated with low sleep disturbance and specific preserved cognitive domains. For controls, accelerated ageing was linked to poor sleep efficiency, a family history of diabetes, and high confectionery/condiment intake. Conversely, decelerated ageing in controls was strongly associated with high physical fitness, Malay ethnicity, increased height, and nutrient-dense diets. Conclusions Explainable ML provides a robust exploratory framework for deciphering complex, interrelated variables associated with telomere attrition. Deciphering the complex biological, clinical, and behavioural profiles associated with accelerated biological ageing via machine learning can help identify highly vulnerable survivors, paving the way for targeted, personalised survivorship care to preserve telomere health.

items.title: Training Machine Learning Prediction of Antibody Thermostability Utilizing PROPERMAB Features and the GDPa4 Dataset
items.abstract_or_text: Antibody drug development is a years-long, costly process. Antibody thermostability is one of the key developability features of an antibody drug that influences its chances of success in development. But, experimental testing such as nanoDSF for large libraries of candidates requires substantial resources. Instead, we evaluated an open-source feature-based machine learning workflow to train a model for antibody stability (Tm1) predictions from sequence and structure-based features. We used PROPERMAB to extract features from a selection of 231 different monoclonal and bispecific antibodies from the GDPa4 nanoDSF dataset. We benchmarked regression and classification models that predict the median first thermal transition temperature (Tm1) from PTS-IF in degrees Celsius for antibodies in the GDPa4 data set from Gingko Datapoints. We trained the models on 184 antibodies and evaluated model performance on 47 held-out antibodies. The three different regression models were ElasticNet, RandomForest, and GradientBoosting. RandomForest achieved the highest reported correlations among the regressors (Pearson r = 0.750, R2 = 0.562). Performance was also evaluated relative to 66.29 degrees Celsius as the threshold for thermostability. The classifier models were LogisticRegression, RandomForest, SupportVector, and GradientBoosting, and classification was defined relative to the training set median of 66.29 degrees Celsius. Thus, above-threshold and below-threshold describe position in this data set, not developability. The best performing model, RandomForest, improved on recall but reduced its precision by recovering two above-threshold antibodies in return for two more false positives. False positives are preferred to false negatives and classification models tended to reduce false negative counts. Most test antibodies also share a parent with a training antibody, so the models predict well for new combinations of known parents but generalization to unknown parents remain unseen However, due to the limited data set used, independent dataset validation is needed before drawing concrete conclusions.

items.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
items.abstract_or_text: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used both a single-turn and a conversational multi-turn text-to-SQL interface over the MIMIC-IV database in a within-subjects design; dialogue analyses additionally drew on interaction logs from 21 healthcare professionals across the main study and two pilot studies. The conversational interface was consistently favored: mean System Usability Scale scores rose from 68.2, near the industry average, to 85.9 (p<0.001), with significant advantages across technology-acceptance constructs including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, self-efficacy, and behavioral intention. In post-study forced-choice comparisons, 93% of participants reported greater overall satisfaction with the conversational interface, 86% preferred it for real-world adoption, and 71% trusted its results more; no participant preferred or trusted the single-turn interface more. Turn-level analysis of 425 logged user turns showed that freely composed queries triggered clarification requests in 24.8% of cases versus 1.8% for predefined, fully specified questions, and 64.3% of clarification episodes stemmed from EHR- or clinical-domain knowledge. Conversational interaction is a practical prerequisite, rather than a convenience, for natural-language EHR access. The frequent need for clarification in realistic clinical queries further underscores the importance of conversational interfaces, while benchmark-style evaluation can substantially underrepresent the ambiguity of real clinical use.

items.title: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
items.abstract_or_text: Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules. Existing machine learning approaches primarily address this problem by generating candidate ligands or scoring individual protein-ligand pairs, but provide limited information about the broader chemical space compatible with a binding pocket. We introduce RangeFinder, an SE(3)-equivariant transformer pocket-level model, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data, that predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context. Using an intersection-over-union objective and evaluation metric (range-IoU), RangeFinder achieves a range-IoU of 0.464 \pm 0.002, outperforming all deployable baselines while requiring only 12.2 ms per pocket. We also quantify our method's ability to reduce the ligand search space while retaining compatible binders; in this regard, RangeFinder achieves a Reduction-Recall F-Score of 0.543 \pm 0.011 --- once again outperforming all deployable baselines. Ablation experiments indicate that RangeFinder's performance depends more strongly on the density and quality of ligand supervision than on any individual input modality or specialized training strategy. Together, these results position RangeFinder as an inexpensive and effective molecular filtering prior, with demonstrated potential in narrowing the ligand search space of target pockets before docking, generation, or synthesis. The code for this project can be found at: https://github.com/alannadels/RangeFinder.

items.title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
items.abstract_or_text: **Purpose:** Ultrasound biometry is widely used across various clinical applications, including prenatal and cardiac examinations, to obtain quantitative measurements by placing calipers at anatomical landmarks. However, these measurements remain subject to interoperator variability as they rely largely on manual caliper placement. Conventional methods often use specialized prediction heads for different ultrasound tasks, whereas vision-language models offer flexibility through text instructions. However, direct coordinate prediction does not explicitly model spatial likelihood distributions, limiting the representation of localization ambiguity. **Methods:** We propose Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection. Inspired by System One decision models, Kev-Bio uses decision representations of the language model to generate queries for each caliper endpoint. These queries are matched against shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived. The model is trained end-to-end using both landmark localization and clinical measurement losses. **Results:** On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error (MRE) of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines in overall performance. **Conclusion:** These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Kev-Bio for ultrasound landmark detection and clinical measurement across different anatomical views. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/moeinheidari7829/Kev-Bio.

items.title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
items.abstract_or_text: Suicide prevention remains a critical public health challenge, and electronic health records (EHRs) provide an opportunity to characterize suicide-related risk indicators using documented clinical, behavioral, medical, and social-contextual information. This paper presents a multidimensional machine learning framework to model and estimate suicide-related outcomes using MIMIC-IV EHR data. We construct clinically motivated diagnosis categories and define a composite outcome from documented codes corresponding to suicidal ideation, suicide attempt, prior suicidal behavior, and intentional self-harm. To address severe class imbalance and reduce age-related confounding, we apply age-matched resampling that retains all positive patients and samples comparison-cohort patients from the same age group. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost classifiers are evaluated before and after resampling with isotonic calibration. The calibrated XGBoost model achieves the strongest matched-cohort performance, outperforming the other evaluated classifiers. SHAP-based interpretation shows that diagnostic burden, depression-related features, age, personality-disorder history, social determinants related to violence, and medical comorbidity contribute to elevated predicted probabilities. Our results demonstrate that combining broad EHR-derived features, age-matched cohort construction, calibration, and feature-level interpretation provides a practical framework for retrospective suicide-related risk modeling.

items.title: Convergent genome- and gene-level constraints shape repeated environmental adaptation in grasses
items.abstract_or_text: Grasses (Poaceae) dominate terrestrial ecosystems and sustain global food security, yet the genomic principles enabling their repeated adaptation to extreme environments remain unresolved. Combining dense phylogenomic sampling, global environmental data, and genomic large language models (gLLMs), we characterize the mutational targets underlying environmental shift across 687 genomes from 561 species spanning 17 climate zones. We identify 17-30 phylogenetically independent transitions into extreme temperature, water, and soil environments, accompanied by convergent shifts in genome-scale molecular properties, including the Nitrogen-to-Carbon balance and the biosynthetic cost of the proteome. Our gLLMs-informed phylogenetic mixed modeling framework identifies 330 genes that repeatedly associated with distinct axes of environmental variation, highlighting the importance of protein modification and localization within extracellular and organellar compartments. Overlaying independent convergent selection tests identifies 27 high-confidence candidates for further characterization. Together, our results show that grass adaptation is canalized by layered constraints at genome-wide and gene-specific scales, producing predictable evolutionary trajectories.

items.title: scRM: A single-cell foundation model trained on scRNA-seq reads
items.abstract_or_text: To our knowledge, scRM is the first single-cell foundation model trained on sequencing reads, demonstrating that raw data pretraining is not only feasible but competitive at a fraction of the computational cost. We anticipate that scaling this framework and exploring alternative architectures will unlock biological information inaccessible to count models and extend the dataset-specific pretraining it already makes possible. The source code is available at https://github.com/altos-labs/scRM.

items.title: NEPTUNE: a neuronal cell death pathway prediction tool used to decipher neurodegeneration using single cell RNA-seq datasets
items.abstract_or_text: In the constantly evolving landscape of cell death mechanisms, much of the literature is dominated by research performed in cancer cells and regenerating cell types. However, neurons differ in that they are non-regenerating and post-mitotic. Therefore, assessing neuronal specific disease biomarkers, including cell death markers, without the bias of non-neuronal or cancerous cells, could provide a more biologically accurate neurodegeneration profile. In this study, we developed the Neuronal cEll death Prediction Tool for Understanding Neurodegenerative Events (NEPTUNE), a user-friendly tool for researchers that bioinformatically identifies neuronal cell death markers from user provided differentially expressed gene lists obtained by single cell RNA sequencing data. We applied NEPTUNE to a publicly available single cell RNA sequencing dataset and analysed the progression of photoreceptor degeneration in the rd1 mouse model of severe retinitis pigmentosa. The analysis interpreted the dataset in a neuronal-specific manner and showed that late-stage photoreceptor death is not purely apoptotic but possibly engages overlapping cell death programmes. From the analysis, the user is provided with publishable graphs and a list of cell death markers with fold change, type of impact, cell death type and a strength score. Overall, our tool provides markers specific to neurodegeneration, allows mapping to known WikiPathways and KEGG pathways, performs GO and KEGG enrichment analysis and plots the data for further analysis, greatly facilitating the study of neuron specific degeneration. The tool can be found at: https://neptune.rgtcarvalholab.com/.

items.title: A Bangla-language retrieval-augmented conversational agent for maternal health in a low-resource setting: design and formative evaluation
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Maternal health information in Bangladesh is difficult to access for women with limited literacy and no English, and perinatal mental health remains under-supported. We designed and formatively evaluated Baby and Me, a Bangla-language conversational agent that retrieves from a curated, physician-reviewed corpus of 247 maternal health articles, segmented into 2,945 indexed passages, and generates responses grounded in the retrieved material. A survey of 72 pregnant and postpartum women established design requirements; Bangla-only language preference was universal among women with no formal or primary education, and a quarter of households reported annual income below one lakh Bangladeshi taka. Candidate model configurations were screened against physician-authored reference answers before deployment. Twenty-four respondents then rated the deployed system: ease of use was highest (mean 4.79 of 5) and clarity strong (4.54), while trust (4.29), concern alignment (4.04) and empathy (4.00) were lower and more dispersed. Interviews indicated that the interface showed users that retrieval had occurred but not whether guidance came from aclinically reviewed source, suggesting that process transparency and source attribution are not interchangeable. As a formative study with a modest sample, a single site and no controlled comparison, this work establishes feasibility rather than effectiveness.

items.title: Patient representation from clinical narratives for early diagnosis of rare diseases: a comparative study on Activated PI3K-δ Syndrome
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS), first described in 2013, is a rare primary immunodeficiency with an estimated prevalence of 1–2 cases per million. Caused by mutations in PIK3CD or PIK3R1 , it leads to immune dysregulation, lymphoproliferation, recurrent infections, and malignancy. Early identification is critical to enable timely initiation of personalized targeted therapies. This study aimed to evaluate whether machine learning applied to clinical narratives could support earlier identification of APDS patients using information extracted from electronic clinical notes. Results: Two approaches derived from clinical notes were evaluated: transformer-based embeddings and phenotype vectors based on UMLS concepts. Machine learning models were trained on 222 patients, including 29 APDS patients. Both approaches achieved strong performance on the full dataset (F1 = 0.82 ± 0.13 and 0.80 ± 0.12, respectively). Phenotype-based analyses included statistical testing, feature importance, ablation studies, and expert review. These analyses identified clinically relevant features including immunodeficiency, adenopathy, lymphopenia, and splenomegaly. Performance remained robust when evaluated on a temporally constrained subset using only pre-diagnosis data (F1 = 0.79 ± 0.14 and 0.74 ± 0.19), supporting the feasibility of earlier detection. Post hoc validation on an independent cohort of 100 patients further supported real-world applicability. Conclusions: Machine learning approaches based on clinical narratives can reliably identify APDS patients, including prior to diagnosis. These findings suggest that such methods could support earlier detection of undiagnosed APDS patients, reducing diagnostic odyssey and improving patient care.

items.title: P2X7 Receptor Signalling as a Danger-Amplifying Hub in Lewy Body Diseases
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Lewy body diseases (LBD), encompassing Parkinson’s disease (PD), Parkinson’s disease dementia (PDD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), are characterised by pathological α-synuclein (αSyn) aggregation, glial dysfunction and a lack of disease-modifying therapies. Converging evidence from α-synucleinopathy models, human neurodegenerative tissue and purinergic target-engagement studies implicates the glial ATP-gated P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) as a potential regulator of inflammatory and proteostatic stress.Main body: This review evaluates P2X7R as a candidate danger-amplifying hub in LBD. We propose that αSyn-rich, ATP-enriched microenvironments may shift glial P2X7R signalling from surveillance and clearance towards maladaptive effector programmes involving excitotoxic vulnerability, NF-κB/MAPK activation, inflammasome engagement, autophagic-lysosomal dysfunction and altered extracellular vesicle biology. We further consider human post-mortem, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging and preclinical evidence, highlighting that direct LBD-specific evidence remains limited and that P2X7R should be interpreted as a context-dependent glial effector receptor rather than a generic marker of inflammation. Conclusions: This framework provides a testable model in which chronic P2X7R activation may contribute to non-cell-autonomous neuronal injury and impaired αSyn handling. P2X7R therefore represents a promising but incompletely validated therapeutic target in LBD. Future studies should prioritise human validation, PET-based disease staging, multicellular αSyn models with cell-type-specific P2RX7 manipulation, and biomarker strategies that distinguish receptor availability from functional target engagement.

items.title: The Findings Workflow: An agentic, collaborative, provenance-tracked framework for scientific data analysis with Claude Code
items.abstract_or_text: Scientists presented with quantitative data often face two related problems: confidence that an analysis is statistically and computationally correct, and provenance sufficient to reproduce the resulting figures and conclusions. Large language models (LLMs) can make sophisticated analyses accessible through a collaborative, conversational interface, but unstructured use can worsen both problems by producing plausible but incorrect results and obscuring the steps that produced them. Here we present the Findings Workflow, a free, open-source Claude Code plugin designed to retain the flexibility of conversational LLM-assisted analysis while placing it within a structured, verifiable, and reproducible environment. The workflow uses staged, gated progression to ensure the science, metadata, and data are understood and tested data loaders are built before downstream analysis begins. Specialized subagents perform statistical analysis, programming, visualization, research, reporting, and validation, with independent review incorporated throughout. The plugin also provides vetted analysis templates, conventions, and methodological guidance that serve as trusted sources of opinion when deciding how analyses should be performed. Scientists remain actively involved throughout, exploring their data and directing the analysis through natural-language conversation, while the workflow supplies structure, verification, and persistent state around that collaboration. Findings are recorded automatically together with the data, code, methods, figures, and provenance needed to reproduce them. We demonstrate the workflow with a worked example that reproduces central findings from a published plasma extracellular vesicle proteomics dataset examining Alzheimer's disease (Mag-Net). Together, these features are designed to make LLM-assisted scientific analysis easier to trust, inspect, and reproduce without sacrificing its conversational and exploratory nature.

items.title: Batch Effect Correction to Enhance Utility of a Publicly Available ALS Proteomics Dataset
items.abstract_or_text: Large, publicly available databases of patient data have been successful in identifying associations between neurodegenerative diseases and biological features that might otherwise go unnoticed. The Answer ALS Consortium is one such database that has generated a rich repository of multi-omic data from people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, large studies can suffer from batch effects that obscure genuine biological signal and prevent experiment reproducibility. In this study, we identified a batch effect in the Answer ALS 1-2 proteomic dataset (508 samples x 3,643 proteins) and corrected the effect using both the internal controls provided by Answer ALS and the batch effect-correction algorithm (BECA) ComBat. We identified a batch effect in the Answer ALS Dataset 1-2 proteomic dataset that, uncorrected, may obscure biology. Proteins MOS and H4 were outliers of expression in the dataset that correlated with the batch effect. Removing MOS and H4 did not correct the effect fully but did reveal new principal component (PC) contributing proteins related to motor neurons and potentially ALS: AINX, NFL, and NFM. The batch differential controls (BDCs) provided by Answer ALS were used to correct samples in their respective batches. ComBat, a well-characterized BECA, was applied to the dataset both before (ComBat-BDC) and after (BDC-ComBat) correction with the BDCs. BDC-ComBat was the only method that successfully reduced batch effect across the entire dataset. This method also preserved four of the top six PC-contributing proteins from the original dataset, including three neuronal proteins, suggesting that the corrected dataset recapitulates biology as well as the variability of the original dataset. Altogether, we produced a version of the Answer ALS proteomic dataset (354 samples by 3,641 proteins) with globally reduced batch effect and protein-level reduced batch effect. This version of the dataset recapitulates the individual protein variability and important neuronal proteins of the original. We also created a workflow for identifying and correcting batch effects that can be applied to other large data repositories.

items.title: Applications of large language model in general practice: a qualitative interview study with professionals and patients
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Workload is increasing in general practice. Large language models (LLMs) are a promising tool that could relieve part of this workload. However, existing studies offer little insight into how professionals and patients want specific LLM applications to be implemented in practice. Objectives: This study aimed to prioritize a broad range of LLM applications in general practice and identify the benefits, risks, and requirements of each application. Methods: We conducted semi-structured one-on-one interviews with 12 general practitioners (GPs), 7 GP assistants, 6 practice nurses, and 6 patient representatives in the Netherlands between October and December 2025. To guide the interviews, we developed a list of 21 LLM applications derived from literature, existing tools, and GP input. Application were divided into 5 categories: administrative tasks, pre-consultation and triage, clinical decision support, management of (chronic) diseases, and patient interaction and communication. Participants discussed and prioritized each application. Transcripts were analyzed with a combined deductive and inductive approach. Results: Priorities for LLM applications differed by group: GPs favored clinical decision support, assistants favored triage, and practice nurses and patient representatives favored chronic disease management. The most prioritized applications were summarizing consultations and triage and urgency classification (high priority 18/31; 58%), followed by clarification of medical information around the consultation (14/31; 45%). The qualitative analysis revealed three recurring considerations when applying LLMs for different tasks. First, participants questioned whether an LLM is needed, as simpler or existing tools may suffice. Second, they questioned whether LLMs relieve workload or create extra work. Third, a possible benefit on workload has to explicitly be weighed against risks such as mistakes, reduced personal care and accessibility, and negative effects on professionals. Conclusions: Professionals and patients see potential for LLM support across many areas of general practice. Realizing this potential requires three steps: critically assessing whether an LLM is the right tool, establishing that it relieves workload, and designing applications so that their benefits outweigh the risks. Our application-level prioritization and analysis provide a starting point for assessment and design.
